description: Exact bounded branch-and-bound set cover by fixing one consecutive-one block at a time.

source.title: Set covering with almost consecutive ones property
source.reference: Discrete Optimization 1(2), 215–228, DOI 10.1016/j.disopt.2004.07.002; summarized in Encyclopedia of Algorithms entry 368
source.algorithm_attribution: Ruf–Schöbel reformulation and branch-and-bound over interval blocks; exact bounded interval-subproblem dynamic program.

input.row_mask_rule: Bit j is 1 iff column j covers the row; rows may have zero bits and represent infeasible valid instances.

output.encoding: [minimum_total_weight], or [-1] for a valid uncoverable instance

workspace.meaning: Conservative fixed per-call budget covering 32 pending states of six row choices each (1,536 bytes in the integer-state ports), row block endpoints, interval and dynamic-program arrays, call frames, and the eight-byte staged result. The maximum search frontier is 19 states because six rows have at most four blocks each.

contract.block_decomposition: Each row is split into its maximal nonempty contiguous runs of 1-bits, in increasing column order.
contract.branch_state: Single-block rows are included in every relaxation; an unassigned multi-block row is omitted, and a branch fixes one of its blocks as the interval constraint for that row.
contract.lower_bound: Solve the exact minimum-weight hitting set for the current consecutive-one interval rows; this is an admissible relaxation of the original set cover.
contract.upper_bound: Start from the lower-bound cover, choose for each still-uncovered original row the block containing its cheapest column (ties: leftmost block), then optimally cover those chosen intervals and union the two covers.
contract.branching: At each node choose the first unassigned multi-block row by input index, then visit its blocks from left to right.
contract.pruning: Use epsilon=0 and prune when the incumbent is no greater than the node lower bound; this yields an exact optimum.
contract.subproblem_method: The bounded ports solve interval hitting subproblems by a shortest-path dynamic program over selected column positions. Optional domination preprocessing and dual-simplex pivot strengthening from the paper are omitted.
contract.tie_rule: Equal-cost interval subproblem covers choose the numerically smaller column bitmask; only optimum cost is emitted.
contract.error_results: Malformed frames return -1. Valid instances with an empty row emit [-1]. Null or undersized output returns -2 without writes.

oracle_method: The primary uses Ruf–Schöbel block branching, interval-relaxation bounds, and an interval shortest-path subsolver. The independent verifier checks all 2^column_count column subsets directly.
